assumptions: Knowledge-only analysis (no web access), June 2026. Assumptions: Brightline is ~40 staff in Dublin split roughly 12 account managers, 8 media buyers, 10 creatives, plus production, finance and leadership; no dedicated CRM admin or RevOps hire; current stack is spreadsheets plus Google Workspace/Slack and ad platforms (Meta, Google Ads, DV360); budget pressure favours low ongoing admin cost; staff are CRM novices except 2-3 AMs with prior Salesforce or HubSpot exposure.
learning_curve_salesforce: Salesforce has the steepest curve of the three. Account managers face an object-heavy model (Leads vs Contacts vs Opportunities, record types, page layouts) that typically takes 4-8 weeks to reach fluency, and the UI rewards configuration work the agency cannot staff. Media buyers gain little out of the box - campaign/ad-ops visibility requires AppExchange add-ons or custom objects, so they will see Salesforce as data-entry overhead. Creatives would rarely log in; licensing them is wasteful. Realistically Brightline needs a part-time admin or partner retainer (EUR 800-1,500/month equivalent) just to keep it usable, which is the classic failure mode for sub-50-person agencies.
learning_curve_hubspot: HubSpot is the gentlest curve. AMs are typically productive in 1-2 weeks: the pipeline board, Gmail/Outlook sidebar, and automatic email/meeting logging match how agency AMs already work, and HubSpot Academy provides free, role-sized certifications that staff can self-serve. Media buyers benefit from native Google Ads, Meta Ads and LinkedIn Ads integrations on Marketing Hub, so attribution data appears without manual entry - the single biggest adoption lever for that role. Creatives only need free seats for visibility into briefs and client context; free-tier seats remove the 'why am I paying to be ignored' resentment. Main friction: AMs must unlearn spreadsheet habits, and reporting beyond canned dashboards takes a power user 3-4 weeks to master.
learning_curve_zoho: Zoho CRM sits in the middle on capability but is deceptively hard to adopt well. The base UI is learnable in 2-3 weeks, but the product's value depends on configuring Zoho's sprawling suite (Campaigns, Analytics, Projects), and the UX is inconsistent across modules, which generates disproportionate support questions. AMs manage, media buyers find the ad-platform integrations (via Zoho Marketing Plus or marketplace connectors) clunkier than HubSpot's, and creatives find the interface dated, which hurts voluntary usage. Lowest licence cost, but the hidden cost is an internal champion spending 2-3 days/month on configuration and answer-desk duty.
training_burden: Estimated time-to-competence per person: HubSpot ~6-8 hours formal training (mostly free HubSpot Academy) plus 2 weeks of nudged usage; Zoho ~12-16 hours plus an internal champion; Salesforce ~20-30 hours plus paid admin support. For 40 people the fully-loaded training delta between HubSpot and Salesforce is roughly 500-800 staff-hours in year one - material for an agency that bills by the hour.
adoption_resistance: Expected resistance, highest first: (1) media buyers, who already live in ad platforms and will reject any tool demanding duplicate data entry - resistance drops sharply if the CRM pulls campaign data automatically (HubSpot strongest here); (2) senior AMs with established personal spreadsheet systems, who resist visibility of their pipelines as much as the tool itself; (3) creatives, who are indifferent rather than hostile - the risk is silent non-use, not complaints. Cultural note for a Dublin agency this size: adoption is decided in the pub-test ('is it annoying?') within the first month; a clunky first fortnight is rarely recovered from.
change_management_recommendations: 1) Phase by role: AMs and leadership in weeks 1-4, media buyers in weeks 4-8 once ad integrations are live and demonstrably zero-extra-typing, creatives on free/read-only seats from week 6. 2) Appoint two internal champions (one AM, one media buyer) with 10% protected time for 90 days; do not outsource champion duty to IT. 3) Migrate only the last 12-18 months of client data - a clean small CRM beats a complete dirty one. 4) Make the CRM the single source of truth by moving one leadership ritual into it immediately (weekly pipeline review run off the CRM dashboard, never a spreadsheet). 5) Set a 60-day kill-the-spreadsheet date, announced upfront. 6) Track adoption weekly: login rate, % of deals with next-step dates, and email-logging rate per AM; intervene with coaching, not mandates, for the first 30 days. 7) Budget a half-day GDPR-handling refresher tied to CRM fields (consent, retention) - Irish staff respond well to framing CRM hygiene as a compliance duty, and it doubles as training reinforcement.
adoption_risk_ranking: Lowest adoption risk: HubSpot. Medium: Zoho CRM (cheap but champion-dependent, dated UX). Highest: Salesforce (needs admin capacity a 40-person agency lacks).
adoption_recommendation_summary: From a pure team-adoption standpoint HubSpot is the clear pick for Brightline: fastest time-to-competence for AMs, native ad-platform integrations that neutralise media-buyer resistance, free seats for creatives, and no dedicated-admin requirement. Confidence 4/5; the residual uncertainty is pricing-tier creep (Marketing Hub Professional costs) which the pricing workstream should weigh.
